problem: A data set consists of the values 12, 15, 18, 22, 25, and 30. What is the population standard deviation of this data set, rounded to the nearest hundredth?

bad.why: Computing the mean, squared deviations, their average, and the square root by hand is the memorized standard-deviation formula Desmos replaces.
Typed into Desmos, the same computation still needs the memorized standard-deviation formula written out term by term; stdevp() of the list needs no formula.

algebraFirst.description: Computes the mean 122/6, each squared deviation, their average, and the square root by hand.

explanationNotes: Explain that 'population' standard deviation is Desmos's stdevp (stdev is the sample version and gives a different number), and that it measures how far the values typically sit from their mean. Round the displayed 6.0736... to the nearest hundredth, 6.07.
notes: Enter the values as a list and read stdevp(L) directly; no manual variance/mean-deviation arithmetic needed.
